title: Patatas Bravas
subtitle: Crispy fried potatoes with spicy tomato sauce and aioli
excerpt: Patatas bravas is the most ordered tapa in Spain: cubed, double-fried potatoes served with a spiced tomato sauce (salsa brava) and often aioli. The combination of crispy potato, smoky-spicy tomato, and rich garlic mayonnaise is the defining tapa experience.
sourceNotes: Patatas bravas (fierce potatoes) originated in Madrid bars in the mid-20th century. The salsa brava distinguishes it from other fried potato dishes: a spiced tomato sauce that varies regionally. Some use a pure chilli and oil sauce, others a tomato base. Both the Madrid and Barcelona versions (which often include aioli) appear in this recipe.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The salsa brava keeps in the fridge for up to 5 days.

content.text: This version oven-roasts rather than deep-fries the potatoes, which gives a crisper result for less effort. The par-boiling step gelatinises the exterior starch, which makes the outside crispy when it hits the hot oil or oven. The salsa brava is a 10-minute hob sauce.

items.prepNote: 4 tbsp for roasting the potatoes, 2 tbsp for the salsa brava
or use sweet paprika if you prefer mild

content.text: Heat the oven to 220°C fan with a roasting tin inside. Bring a large pan of salted water to the boil. Add the potato cubes and boil for 5 minutes. They should be slightly softened but still holding together. Drain and steam dry for 2 minutes.

Shake the drained potatoes in the colander to roughen the edges. This increases the crispy surface area. Tip into the hot roasting tin with the olive oil. Season with salt. Toss to coat and roast for 30 to 35 minutes, turning twice, until deep golden and crispy.

Heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute until softened. Add the smoked paprika and hot paprika and cook for 30 seconds. Pour in the passata. Season with salt and the white wine vinegar. Simmer for 10 minutes until thick. Taste and adjust.
Pile the hot potatoes onto a serving dish. Spoon the salsa brava over. If serving with aioli, add it in dollops alongside. Serve immediately with cocktail sticks.

items.cause: Oven or roasting tin was not hot enough, or potatoes were too wet when they went in
items.fix: The tin must be hot before the potatoes go in. Steam the drained potatoes thoroughly, and shake them to roughen the surface. Wet potatoes steam rather than roast.
